message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Use the report, not the notes. The notes have two errors: the 12.5% was the nine-month figure, and output per worker fell rather than staying flat.

**Suggested sentences:**

> The per-hour productivity gain persisted but narrowed over time: output per actual hour was 12.5% higher than in control offices at nine months and 8.5% higher at 24 months (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%; system logs). Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per full-time employee was 3.4% lower than in controls at 24 months, though the confidence interval (−8.1% to +1.5%) does not rule out no change.

**Notes vs report:**

| Item | Team notes | Report (Table 1) |
|---|---|---|
| Per-hour gain at 24 months | "held steady at 12.5%" | +8.5% (12.5% was at nine months) |
| Output per worker | unchanged (0%) | −3.4% (CI −8.1 to +1.5) |
| Meeting hours | roughly halved | 7.4 → 3.9 (−47%); controls 7.2 → 7.0. Fair summary |

Two other points:
- The report's own per-FTE interval is −8.1 to +1.5. Quote that rather than my earlier back-of-envelope range.
- It's worth correcting the team notes so the errors don't propagate into other papers. They also affect the earlier draft briefing, which claimed output per worker would rise.
